# Scope for Linux: full text

Scope for Linux (also called Scope) is a free, open-source app manager. It lists apps, command-line tools and games from APT, Snap, Flatpak, AppImage, uv, pipx, Cargo, npm, Bun, Steam and JetBrains Toolbox in one searchable list. Every update or uninstall starts with a plan that shows the exact commands. Scope runs them only after the user confirms. Written in Rust with Zed's GPUI, no webview. Ubuntu on x86-64 is the primary target. Current version: 0.3.8. License: MIT. Source: https://github.com/khurrambhutto/scope

## What Scope does

Most Linux users install software from several places: the Ubuntu archive, the Snap Store, Flathub, AppImages from download pages, and developer tools from uv, pipx, Cargo, npm or Bun. Each source has its own list and its own command, so a user rarely knows everything that is installed.

Scope reads all of them and shows them in one list. The default list shows recognizable apps and tools. Show all reveals packages hidden from the default list. Protected packages stay locked even with Show all on.

Users can switch between installed apps and available updates, search by app or package name, filter by source, inspect what an app occupies on disk, and rescan. To install a downloaded .deb or AppImage, choose Open With → Scope and review the installation preview.

## How a change works

1. Plan. Scope builds a preview with the exact commands, for example `pkexec env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o APT::Get::AutomaticRemove=false purge -y -- <package>`. APT transactions are simulated first. Nothing runs yet.
2. Confirm. The user reads the plan and confirms or cancels. A plan works once and expires after five minutes.
3. Revalidate. Right before it runs, Scope checks that the package is still installed, that an update's version has not changed, and that the deny-list still allows the action. APT simulations must match the preview. If Scope cannot confirm the state, it stops.
4. Run. Admin commands go through the Polkit dialog. Progress appears at the bottom of the window. Only one package operation runs at a time.

## Supported sources and actions

| Source | Uninstall | Update |
| --- | --- | --- |
| APT | `pkexec env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o APT::Get::AutomaticRemove=false purge -y -- <pkg>` | `pkexec env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt install -y <pkg>` |
| Snap | `pkexec snap remove <pkg>` | `pkexec snap refresh <pkg>` |
| Flatpak user | `flatpak uninstall -y --user <id>` | `flatpak update -y --user <id>` |
| Flatpak system | `pkexec flatpak uninstall -y --system <id>` | `pkexec flatpak update -y --system <id>` |
| uv tool | `uv tool uninstall <pkg>` in the recorded tool and bin roots | `uv tool upgrade <pkg>` |
| pipx | `pipx uninstall <environment>` | `pipx upgrade <environment>` with recorded pip options |
| Cargo | `cargo uninstall --root <root> <pkg>` | `cargo install --root <root>` with the original source and build settings |
| npm global | `npm uninstall --global --prefix <prefix> <pkg>` | `npm update --global --prefix <prefix> <pkg>` |
| Bun global | `bun remove --global <pkg>` | `bun update --global <pkg>` |
| AppImage in ~/AppImages (Scope or Gear Lever) | moves the AppImage, its launchers and icons to the Trash; app data only when opted in | downloads the published update over HTTPS, verifies its digest, replaces in place |
| Other AppImages, unmanaged launchers | discovery only | discovery only |
| Steam games | read-only | Open in Steam |
| JetBrains Toolbox IDEs | read-only | Open Toolbox |

User tools are managed as the user, never as root. Update availability depends on the source and how the app was installed. Scope never edits the dpkg or apt databases directly.

## Safety

- Preview first. Every destructive action builds a plan, applied only once and only within five minutes.
- Revalidate before running. Scope fails closed when it cannot verify the state.
- Simulate APT with LC_ALL=C. Scope rejects transactions that would remove or purge a protected package, and requires the same simulation right before apply.
- APT uninstall purges package configuration with autoremove disabled. Personal settings and data in the home directory remain. Scope never runs autoremove.
- Deny-list. Critical APT packages (including Ubuntu desktop metapackages and the Ubuntu session), kernel images, lib* packages matched by a heuristic, Snap runtimes, and AppImage paths outside ~/AppImages are protected.
- No passwords in the app. Commands that need root run through pkexec and the standard Polkit dialog.
- No shell. Commands are fixed argument lists.
- Trash. Files Scope removes itself go to the Trash with gio trash, with a fallback to ~/.local/share/Trash.
- Verified updates. Official .deb builds check a minisign-signed SHA-256 manifest before they install a new version.

## Install

Ubuntu, x86-64:

```bash
sudo apt install ./scope_0.3.8_amd64.deb
```

A portable x86-64 build is available as Scope-0.3.8-x86_64.AppImage. Make it executable with chmod +x, then launch it. Most AppImages need libfuse2t64; AppImage integration needs squashfs-tools. Releases include SHA256SUMS and its minisign signature.

The package is named scope. Remove it with `sudo apt remove scope`. Removing Scope does not remove the apps it lists.

Build from source needs Rust stable and build-essential, pkg-config, libfontconfig1-dev, libx11-dev, libx11-xcb-dev, libxcb1-dev, libxkbcommon-dev, libxkbcommon-x11-dev, libwayland-dev and wayland-protocols. Then run `cargo run`.

## Not yet

- .rpm release packages
- Fedora and Arch package-manager support
- Whole-system cleanup and disk usage views

## Comparison

Synaptic manages APT packages only. GNOME Software, KDE Discover and Flathub are app stores that show what their catalogs offer. Scope starts from what is already installed, across system packages, AppImages and developer tools, and makes the plan the thing the user approves.

## Who made it

Scope is built by Khurram Bhutto (https://github.com/khurrambhutto). Source and issues: https://github.com/khurrambhutto/scope.

## FAQ

Q: What is Scope?
A: A free, open-source Linux app manager that lists apps, tools and games from twelve sources in one list, with a preview before every update or uninstall.

Q: Does Scope ask for my password?
A: No. Admin actions use the standard Polkit dialog through pkexec. Scope never sees or stores the password.

Q: Can Scope remove critical system packages by accident?
A: The deny-list protects critical packages. It is checked at preview and again before apply, and APT transactions that would take a protected package with them are rejected.

Q: What does uninstall remove?
A: The app and what its package manager installed. APT uninstall purges package configuration but keeps home-directory data. Snap may keep a recovery snapshot.

Q: Which distributions are supported?
A: Ubuntu on x86-64 first, with a .deb and an AppImage. Other distributions can use the AppImage or build from source.

Q: Is Scope free?
A: Yes. It is released under the MIT License.
